summary: Sanders County, MT cupola cabin 3 mi NE of Trout Creek; built 1920 for the Forest Service, destroyed 1955; the association now lists the site as ground only, gone.

facts.design: 12 by 12 foot standard Forest Service cabin with a six-foot cupola and glass on all sides
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1955 per firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks the site as a ground site that is gone. No source describes what remains.

staffing.status: Staffed in 1921 by A. E. Clark and in 1930 by Tom Churwell; no later staffing found in the sources read

events.note: Telephone line poles set toward the '20-Odd lookout', which suggests use of the site before the 1920 cabin
Cabin built in 1920 per firelookout.com; March 1920 contractor report and September 1920 inspection report in the Sanders County Independent-Ledger (quoted on Forest Lookouts)
A. E. Clark, lookout in 1921; a Sept 8, 1921 Ledger item says he had recently left the peak and was due to start planting-camp work
Tom Churwell took up the lookout's duties in June 1930
Destroyed in 1955; the Forest Lookouts page credits the date to Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and the March to September 1920 Ledger items put the cabin in 1920. A 1917 telephone-line item and a Flathead Courier item from September 1920 (saying the design was built a year earlier as an experiment) point to earlier use or a trial build. The story reports the 1920 cabin and notes the earlier references without settling the question.
firelookout.com gives 3 miles northeast of Trout Creek; the Forest Lookouts page says north of Trout Creek. The story uses the firelookout.com distance and direction.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: status gone, kind ground, agency Kootenai NF. The start date conflicts across sources (1917 telephone poles and the Courier's 'built a year ago as an experiment' versus the 1920 cabin); the story gives 1920 as the cabin date and notes the earlier references. The 1955 destruction date rests on firelookout.com and a Kresek citation quoted on Forest Lookouts; no newspaper report of the 1955 loss was found. No source describes the peak today or access, so the access key is omitted. The photo has no date on the page. One WebSearch and about four page reads used.
